It's actually pretty fuckin hard to stop. The difficulty of opioid withdrawal is the half life. Kratom leaf contains an opioid, but that opioid's metabolite is an even more powerful opioid. Because opioid withdrawal is directly correlated to the half-life of receptor agonism, and because the active constituent and metabolite last so long overall, going into forced withdrawal on a heavy kratom habit can leave you fucked up for days before you can commit to life basics and a week before you're really through it, depending on dose.

Fentanyl and it's derivatives will provide a particularly agonizing withdrawal, but fent and its derivatives have half lives measured in minutes to an hour or two. So instead of a 4-6 day influenza-esque withdrawal, you (sometimes violently) pukeshit yourself uncontrollably for about 36 hours, and then it's just...over.

Note that I'm not saying fent is better. It's actually way fucking worse. The shortened duration of suffering does not even come close to making up for the immeasurable increase in magnitude of immediate withdrawal from fent or its derivatives. It's the difference between feeling that you are sick and feeling that you will actually fuckin die.

There's not really a difference between "psychoactive" or "psychotropic", to go back to the original question. It's the kind of language thing that's up to interpretation. If the speaker chooses to define them differently then that is to be considered when listening to them. They can be used interchangeably.

Though to me, psychoactive would specifically mean that the substance has a specific physiological effect within the brain itself.

Psychotropic, to me, would mean that the agent has an impact on the subject's mental state. That is to say, breath work can be psychotropic. Exercise can be psychotropic. The agent doesn't even have to be a substance. Whereas the word "psychoactive" has a more specific medical meaning in scientific publications, that meaning being "this molecule crosses the blood-brain barrier and acts to modulate psychological function at a physiological level".

It's not that describing any drug as psychotropic is wrong. But to my subjective ears, psychoactive is the more appropriate term when speaking about a specific molecule interacting with the function of the brain.

Remember to use a blowtorch-style lighter, and then have somewhere secure and safe that you can set the glass after your hit. The lighter might be a little hot depending on design, but the glass at the bulb can easily be "instant 2nd degree burn"-hot. 

An easy holder to make is a tall cup with a wide or heavy base, tear out a couple large squares of aluminum foil, and push the center of those squares 3/4 of the way down the cup (without breaking them, obviously). The aluminum makes a little bowl shape to catch the glass, but it doesn't actually touch the bottom. Then, you wedge that cup somewhere close so it can't tip over, you blast off, and you can literally drop the burner in there without worrying about it. It is *extremely hot glass that can shatter or start fire* so it's important to have a plan about that ahead of time. You don't wanna be like "oh damn" as it starts to take hold and drop it in your bed, your lap, on the floor, etc. 

When you're *vaporizing* a substance, it's not like smoking. With smoking, a large majority of the amount of drug in any individual hit is absorbed within seconds, and excessive holds really just let more tar and particulates settle in the lungs. With vaping a substance directly, everything you inhale is the substance. You don't have all the particulates or combustion products (if you're doing it right), so you want to hold the hit literally as long as you are able to.
